name: Allan Alcorn

NOT AN ATARI HIT / NOT A COLLISION WITH p222. PI instruction: Alcorn was an Atari EMPLOYEE; a5 attaches to his own venture. CHM: Bushnell "hired Al as one of the first employees in 1972". Wikipedia and the PI treat Silicon Gaming as his cofounded venture; S-1 lists Morse/Fell from inception and Alcorn as joining Nov 1993 -- still his own venture under the PI frame, not Atari. a5: Silicon Gaming rev10 pinned at calendar 1997. name: Nolan Bushnell

In 1972, the name was changed to Atari". NOT A COLLISION WITH p221: Bushnell cofounded Atari; Alcorn was employee #3. Different own-venture events. a1: CHM "Born on February 5, 1943, in Clearfield, Utah". Wikipedia same day; encyclopedia.com says Ogden -- year is uncontested. a2: CHM "After graduating in 1968, he landed a job at Ampex Corporation". encyclopedia.com: "Bushnell attended college at the University of Utah, where he earned an engineering degree in 1968". CONFLICT: University of Utah Continuum alumni magazine (2013) prints "Bushnell BS'69". Two independent sources (CHM, encyclopedia.com) give 1968; recorded 1968 at medium. a3/a4: first domain work = first venture. CHM: "In 1970, Bushnell cofounded Syzygy, which created Computer Space". Ampex after 1968 was video-recording equipment, not coin-op games. Nutting Associates employment on Computer Space is 1971 (Slate/Wikipedia) and post-dates the Syzygy founding. Syzygy was renamed Atari on incorporation 27 June 1972 (same entity). a5: BOUNDED rev10 1972-1974. Lower: Atari/Syzygy cannot earn before it exists; CHM dates the Atari name to 1972; Wikipedia/Game Developer date incorporation 27 June 1972. Upper: TIME's own 1 April 1974 "Space-Age Pinball" article, quoted on TIME Techland 29 Nov 2012: "Typical of the new games is Pong, a popular version of electronic table tennis manufactured by two-year-old Atari, Inc. (estimated fiscal 1974 revenue: $14 million)". python3 -m src.cpi 1974 output: rev10 ($10,000,000 constant 2026) = $1,531,327. $14M is ~9x the 1974 bar. Same TIME piece: "Atari sold some 8,500 games to U.S. amusement parlors and other businesses last year" (i.e. 1973) at "a high purchase price (about $1,100)". Game Developer 2007 (Steve Fulton, citing Bushnell): "By March of 1973, Atari had made a little over $3.2 million dollars" -- already above the 1973 bar of $1,379,126 -- but "made" is ambiguous (revenue vs earnings) so the TIME fiscal-1974 revenue figure is the upper pin. Span is two years, not stretched. Founding year used as lower bound because no sourced calendar-year figure sits below the bar. python3 -m src.cpi 1972 output: rev10 = $1,298,366; python3 -m src.cpi 1973 output: rev10 = $1,379,126. Warner 1976 $28M sale is BARRED as the a5 fallback because an earlier rev10 crossing is known. Used as a6. a6: CHM "In 1976, Bushnell sold Atari to Warner Communications in a deal worth $28 million". encyclopedia.com same $28 million. python3 -m src.cpi 1976 output: acq50 = $8,836,968. $28M is well above. SERIAL: Syzygy/Atari is the first company; Computer Space's ~$3M sales were Nutting Associates', not Syzygy's.
